title: I Would, but Cannot Sing
description: I Would, but Cannot Sing in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 126, “The good that I would I do not. Rom 7”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I would, but can-not sing, Guilt has un-tuned my voice; The ser-pent sin's en-ven-omed sting Has poi-soned all my joys.

lines: I know the Lord is nigh,
For Satan meets me when I try,
This stony heart can ne'er relent
No arguments have pow'r to move
A soul so base as mine.
I know what he appoints is best,
I would, but cannot, Lord relieve,
My help must come from thee!
Yet the desire is something good,
For which my praise is due.
I was as destitute of will,
As now I am of pow'r.
Wilt thou not crown, at length,
And with a will, afford me strength
In all thy ways to run.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
